extra_zh.title: 对标竞品地图
extra_zh.body:
缺件先说：Product Hunt 的评论正文本次抓取失败（0 条），所以这张地图不引用 PH 的 Similar Products，名单来自两处——官方产品线自身的重叠（Make / Sites / Dev Mode 各有一段对手），以及 G2 与第三方评测里用户说实际换去的地方。

谁抢同一个需求抢同一段链路用户实际迁移
SketchMac 上做设计稿画布 + 组件 + 切图存量还在，但协作要外挂；老用户被 Figma 的多人同文件拉走（评论里几乎不提 Sketch，说明它已不是主要比较对象）
Penpot要自主可控的设计协作开源 + 自托管 + 浏览器协作预算与合规敏感段被它接走；[推断] 政企与自建需求是它的主场
Framer设计完想直接上线画布 → 托管 → CMS双向：要上线的人在 Framer，要团队协作的人在 Figma；实测（燃冰）原话点明差异——Framer 偏落地，Figma 偏设计资料沉淀与代码原型导出
Webflow营销站与专业建站画布 + 托管 + CMS + SEO 深度技术 SEO 有硬要求的团队留在 Webflow（robots.txt、静态文件可控）
Lovable / v0 / Claude Code一句话出可跑的界面语言 → 代码 → 部署增量团队可能从代码起手，压根不进设计工具——这是唯一能「绕开」而不只是「抢走」的一路
Canva非设计师要做图模板 + 拖拽 + 品牌套件营销物料段的分流；Figma 用 Buzz 反向切进去（[推断]）

读法：Figma 在地图正中，四面都有对手，但没有一个对手同时具备「多人同文件 + 组件体系 + 交付链路」三件套。真正危险的不是被抢，是被绕开。

extra_zh.title: 竞品技术底座
extra_zh.body:
产品底座设计到落地的接缝
Figma自研的浏览器渲染引擎（WebGL/Canvas 混合）+ 实时协作同步（CRDT 系思路）+ 云端文件存储 + 插件沙箱 + Dev Mode 代码映射 + MCP 服务接缝在「导出之后」：同一文件切 Dev Mode 给代码与规格，Sites 想直接把设计发上线（beta）
SketchmacOS 原生（Metal）+ 本地 .sketch 文件 + 插件；协作需第三方（如 Abstract）接缝是文件交换，版本靠人工约定
PenpotWeb 技术栈（Clojure/ClojureScript）+ SVG 原生 + 可自托管接缝是自建部署与内网合规
Framer自研画布 + 自建托管与 CDN + 内置 CMS / 分析 / 本地化接缝被抹平：画布即生产环境，没有导出这一步（也因此没有代码导出）
Webflow自研可视化 CSS 引擎 + 托管 + 更强导出接缝在 CSS 语义可控 + 可导出
Lovable / v0LLM 生成 React / Tailwind，跑在托管预览环境，源码可导出接缝就是代码：生成物天生是工程产物

[推断] 真护城河不在模型层（模型能力外部可得，Make 的生成质量不是它最难复制的东西），而在「实时协作的同步内核 + 文件格式成为行业默认 + 组件资产沉淀」三者的耦合。这三样都得靠时间与用户习惯堆，买不到也追不快。反过来说，AI 生成这条能力最容易被追平，所以它把 AI 做成 credits 而不是主卖点——这是清醒的。

extra_zh.title: 可迁移的机会（我的判断）
extra_zh.body:
1. 把「加入即计费」做成事前提示——有人被拉进文件之前，先显示他会占哪类席位、本月多花多少，默认只给评论权。G2 两条独立投诉（14 个月、重复收费不退）都出在这里；对一个一人的投资工具产品，这就是「用户不知道钱怎么涨的」那一类失败，最伤信任。最轻，一个弹层加一次确认。
  2. 把 credits 变成可见预算条——生成前显示预估消耗与余额，接近上限时警告。实测（燃冰）第一次用完免费额度是没有预警的；一人公司可预期比便宜重要。
  3. 把「生成」做成带 diff 的审阅——每次 agent 改动列出动了哪些组件与状态。实测的关键一句是「可以改图层」，但没告诉人改了什么；审阅能力决定人敢不敢放手。
  4. 把文件所有权与个人解耦——团队可强制接管离职成员的文件，停用前给导出提醒。这条对代理商是成交门槛。

四个里哪个最轻？第 1 个：不需要动产品架构，只改一个默认值和一句提示。哪个最贵也最值？第 4 个：它决定的是「敢不敢把整个设计资产放进来」，而这正是订阅制最想要的答案。

extra_zh.title: 流量与变现拆解
extra_zh.body:
钱从三方出：做设计的人（Full 席位 16 / 55 / 90 美元）、只读代码的人（Dev 12 / 25 / 35）、只评论的人（Collab 3 / 5 / 5）；再叠一层按量计费的 AI credits（Full 席位 3,000 / 3,500 / 4,250，Dev 与 Collab 500；超出加购或按量）。

产品计价单位起步价（本次可核实口径）免费档口径说明
Figma席位（Full / Dev / Collab）Professional 年付 16 / 12 / 3 美元每月；Org 55 / 25 / 5；Ent 90 / 35 / 5有（Starter：草稿不限、credits 150/日上限 500/月）官方定价页，本次直接抓取
Framer站点 + 席位 + credits第三方口径 10–15 美元（Basic）/ 30–45（Pro），编辑器约 20 美元有第三方转述，月付与年付口径混用，只作量级
Webflow站点第三方口径约 15 美元/月起有（受限站点）第三方转述
Sketch编辑席位第三方口径约 12 美元/编辑/月（年付）无免费档（试用）第三方转述
Penpot自托管 / 云开源免费，商业版另计有项目公开信息
Lovable / v0订阅 + 用量含免费层，具体档位未逐项核实有未核实，不编数字

价格结论（我的判断）：单人场景下 Figma 的 16 美元与 Framer 的 10–15、Sketch 的 12 是同一量级，不贵；贵在「按人涨」。五个人的团队按 Figma 算 5×16＝80 美元，按站点计价的 Framer 只要一个站点加一两个编辑席位；但 Framer 的编辑席位也按人收，团队一多同样陡。所以真正的差别不是单价，是计价轴：Figma 按人头，Framer 按站点。谁的团队里「做设计的人少、看的人多」，谁的账单就轻——这恰好解释了 Figma 为什么要拆出 Dev 与 Collab 两类席位。

流量吃长尾：Community 公开文件与设计系统是可搜索的入口，作品集与设计教育持续供人，产品发布（PH 36 次 Launch、15K 关注）负责波峰。变现三段：订阅（广度）→ 席位类型（厚度）→ credits 与加购（深度）。最脆的一根梁是「分享免费、协作可能计费」与「文件归个人所有」这两条同时成立：前者让账单自己长出来，后者让资产归属说不清——G2 的低分几乎全落在这两根梁上。

extra_en.title: Competitive map
extra_en.body:
Missing piece first: the Product Hunt review body returned 0 items this run, so this map does not use PH Similar Products. It comes from two places — overlaps inside Figma own product line (Make, Sites and Dev Mode each meet rivals) and where users say they actually go in G2 and third-party reviews.

WhoSame needSame link in the chainActual migration
SketchDraw the interface on a MacCanvas, components, slicingStill has an installed base, but collaboration needs bolt-ons; its users were pulled away by multiplayer in one file (reviews barely mention Sketch, which suggests it is no longer the comparison)
PenpotDesign collaboration with ownershipOpen source, self-hosted, browser collaborationTakes the budget and compliance-sensitive segment; [inference] public sector and self-hosted needs are its home
FramerDesign and publish directlyCanvas, hosting, CMSTwo-way: publishing goes to Framer, team collaboration stays in Figma. My test framed it as Framer leaning delivery, Figma leaning accumulated design material and exportable code prototypes
WebflowMarketing sites and professional buildsCanvas, hosting, CMS, deep SEOTeams with hard technical SEO requirements stay (robots.txt and static files under their control)
Lovable / v0 / Claude CodeOne sentence to a running interfaceLanguage, code, deployNew teams may start from code and never enter a design tool — the only path that routes around rather than competes
CanvaNon-designers making visualsTemplates, drag and drop, brand kitsSiphons marketing material; Figma pushes back with Buzz ([inference])

How to read it: Figma sits in the middle and faces rivals on four sides, but none of them holds all three of multiplayer in one file, a component system and a handoff chain. The real danger is not being out-competed, it is being routed around.

extra_en.title: Rivals technical foundations
extra_en.body:
ProductFoundationSeam from design to delivery
FigmaOwn browser rendering engine (WebGL and Canvas hybrid), real-time sync, cloud file storage, plugin sandbox, Dev Mode code mapping, MCP serviceThe seam sits after export: switch the same file into Dev Mode for code and specs, and Sites tries to publish straight from design (beta)
SketchNative macOS (Metal), local .sketch files, plugins; collaboration via third parties such as AbstractThe seam is file exchange; versions are agreed by convention
PenpotWeb stack (Clojure/ClojureScript), native SVG, self-hostableThe seam is self-hosting and internal compliance
FramerOwn canvas, own hosting and CDN, built-in CMS, analytics, localisationThe seam is erased: canvas is production, so there is no export step — and no code export
WebflowOwn visual CSS engine, hosting, stronger exportThe seam is controllable CSS semantics plus export
Lovable / v0LLM generates React / Tailwind into a hosted preview, source exportableThe seam is code itself: the output is an engineering artifact by birth

[inference] The real moat is not the model layer — model capability is externally available, and Make generation quality is not the hardest thing here to copy. The moat is the coupling of a real-time collaboration core, a file format that became the industry default, and accumulated component assets. All three are built from time and habit; none can be bought quickly. Conversely, generation is the easiest capability to match, which is exactly why Figma meters AI as credits instead of leading with it.

extra_en.title: Transferable opportunities (my judgement)
extra_en.body:
1. Show the cost of joining before joining — before someone is added to a file, show which seat type they occupy and what it adds to this month bill, defaulting to comment-only. Both G2 complaints (14 months, duplicate charges with no refund) live here; for a one-person investment tool, this is the users cannot see how the number grew failure, and it is the most corrosive kind. Lightest: one modal and one confirmation.
  2. Turn credits into a visible budget bar — show estimated spend and balance before generation, warn near the limit. In my test the free allowance ran out with no warning; for a one-person company predictability beats cheapness.
  3. Make generation reviewable with diffs — list which components and states each agent change touched. My test noted the layers stay editable, but nothing told me what had changed, and reviewability is what decides whether a person dares let go.
  4. Decouple file ownership from the individual — let a team take over files from departing members and prompt export before deactivation. For agencies this is the deal-breaker.

Which of the four is lightest? The first: no architectural change, one default value and one sentence. Which is the most expensive and most valuable? The fourth: it decides whether a team dares put its entire design asset inside, which is the answer a subscription business most wants.

extra_en.title: Traffic and monetisation breakdown
extra_en.body:
Money comes from three parties: people who design (Full seat at 16 / 55 / 90 USD), people who only read code (Dev at 12 / 25 / 35), and people who only comment (Collab at 3 / 5 / 5). On top sits metered AI: credits of 3,000 / 3,500 / 4,250 on Full seats and 500 on Dev and Collab, with add-ons or pay-as-you-go beyond.

ProductBilling unitEntry price (verifiable this run)Free tierBasis
FigmaSeat (Full / Dev / Collab)Professional annual 16 / 12 / 3 USD per month; Org 55 / 25 / 5; Enterprise 90 / 35 / 5Yes (Starter: unlimited drafts, 150 credits/day capped at 500/month)Official pricing page, captured directly
FramerSite plus seats plus creditsThird-party figures 10–15 (Basic) / 30–45 (Pro) USD, editors around 20YesThird-party relay mixing monthly and annual, order of magnitude only
WebflowSiteThird-party around 15 USD per monthYes (restricted site)Third-party relay
SketchEditor seatThird-party around 12 USD per editor per month, annualNo free tier (trial only)Third-party relay
PenpotSelf-hosted / cloudOpen source free; commercial edition separateYesProject public information
Lovable / v0Subscription plus usageFree layer exists; tiers not itemised hereYesNot verified, no numbers invented

Price verdict (my judgement): for one person, 16 USD at Figma sits in the same band as Framer at 10–15 and Sketch at 12 — not expensive. What is expensive is that it scales per person. A five-person team pays 5 × 16 = 80 USD at Figma, while a site-priced Framer needs one site plus one or two editor seats; but Framer editor seats are also per person, so it steepens too. The real difference is not the unit price, it is the billing axis: Figma counts heads, Framer counts sites. Whichever team has few designers and many viewers carries a lighter bill — which is precisely why Figma split out Dev and Collab seats.

Traffic comes mostly from the long tail: Community files and design systems are searchable entries, portfolios and design education keep feeding people in, and launches (36 on Product Hunt, 15K followers) supply the peaks. Monetisation runs in three stages: subscription for breadth, seat types for depth per account, credits and add-ons for depth per use. The weakest beam is that sharing is free while collaboration may cost, at the same time as files are owned by individuals: the first lets invoices grow on their own, the second makes ownership unclear — and almost every low G2 score lands on those two beams.
